test_prompts.title: Piano vs Forte Baseline
test_prompts.concept: 가장 기본적인 다이내믹 대비 — piano(여리게)와 forte(세게)를 명시적으로 지정했을 때 실제 음량 차이가 나는가?
test_prompts.corpus_reference: piano(악기명과 혼동 가능), forte(9회), soft(89회), loud(45회)
test_prompts.sp: Rock band piece with extreme volume contrast between sections. The verse is played piano, very soft and delicate. Drums use only brushes. Guitar plays clean fingerpicking at low volume. Bass plays gently with fingers. The vocalist whispers. The chorus explodes into forte, loud and powerful. Drums switch to full kit with heavy hitting. Guitar switches to distorted power chords at maximum volume. Bass plays aggressively with a pick. The vocalist belts at full power. The contrast between verse and chorus should be dramatic and immediate. Electric guitar, electric bass, drum kit, male vocals. 120 BPM in E minor. 4/4 time. Rock production.

Rising in the silence

BUT WHEN THE STORM ARRIVES
THERE IS NO PLACE TO HIDE

AND WE COME ALIVE

[Verse 2 — piano, soft]
(whispering again)
Back to silence once again
Fingers barely touching strings

[Chorus — forte, loud]
(belting, maximum power)
BUT WHEN THE STORM ARRIVES
WE RISE WE RISE WE RISE

[Outro — piano, fading]
(whisper, disappearing)
In the quiet...

test_prompts.title: Six-Step Gradation
test_prompts.concept: 6단계 다이내믹(ppp→pp→p→f→ff→fff) — 코퍼스 0회인 극단 다이내믹을 포함한 전체 스펙트럼
test_prompts.corpus_reference: ppp(0회), pp(0회), p(악기명 혼동), f(0회), ff(0회), fff(0회) — 전부 데드존
test_prompts.sp: Solo piano piece presenting six dynamic levels as a continuous staircase. The piece begins at pianississimo, the softest possible touch, barely audible, like hearing a piano from three rooms away. It gradually steps up to pianissimo, still very quiet but now each note has definition. Then piano, a normal soft playing level. Then forte, a confident full sound. Then fortissimo, powerful and resonant, the piano singing at full voice. Finally fortississimo, the loudest possible attack, hammering the keys with maximum force, the piano almost percussive. Each dynamic level sustains for eight bars playing the same simple melody, so the only variable is volume. Grand piano. 80 BPM. 4/4 time. Concert hall with natural acoustics.

(the piano screaming)

[Descent]

(the staircase in reverse)

[Final]

(silence reclaims the room)

test_prompts.title: Sforzando and Forte-Piano
test_prompts.concept: 순간적 다이내믹 표기 — sfz(갑자기 강하게)와 fp(세게 치고 즉시 여리게) — 코퍼스 0회 데드존
test_prompts.corpus_reference: sfz(0회), fp(0회), sforzando(0회), forte-piano(0회) — 완전 데드존
test_prompts.sp: String quartet piece built entirely on sudden dynamic attacks. The violins, viola, and cello play a sustained quiet passage at pianissimo, then without warning hit a sforzando accent — a single note played with sudden explosive force before immediately returning to quiet. This sforzando interruption happens unpredictably throughout the piece. The second section introduces forte-piano markings where every phrase begins with a loud attack that instantly drops to soft, like a bell being struck then muted. The third section combines both: sforzando accents interrupt a forte-piano texture. First violin, second violin, viola, cello. 72 BPM in D minor. 4/4 time. Intimate chamber music recording.

(the last crack, then nothing)

test_prompts.title: The Long Crescendo
test_prompts.concept: 32마디에 걸친 점진적 크레셴도 — Suno가 긴 호흡의 음량 변화를 지속할 수 있는가?
test_prompts.sp: Orchestral rock piece built on a single thirty-two bar crescendo from complete silence to maximum volume. The piece starts with a single acoustic guitar note played at the softest possible volume. Every two bars, a new instrument joins and the overall volume increases slightly. Bar 1: solo acoustic guitar, barely audible. Bar 8: bass guitar enters quietly. Bar 12: hi-hat only, tapping softly. Bar 16: piano joins with single notes. Bar 20: full drum kit enters at moderate volume. Bar 24: electric guitar with distortion, volume increasing. Bar 28: all instruments at forte. Bar 32: every instrument at maximum volume, full distortion, crashing cymbals, the loudest possible moment. The crescendo must be continuous and gradual, never stepping back. 100 BPM in A minor. 4/4 time.

test_prompts.title: Subito Piano
test_prompts.concept: subito piano — 최대 음량에서 갑자기 최소 음량으로 전환. 점진적이 아닌 즉각적 다이내믹 전환
test_prompts.corpus_reference: subito(0회), suddenly soft(0회), drop(악기 의미 혼용)
test_prompts.sp: Hard rock song with three dramatic subito piano moments. The band plays at full volume fortissimo for sixteen bars: heavy distorted guitar riffs, pounding drums, screaming vocals. Then without any transition or fade, the music drops instantly to the softest possible level — subito piano. Acoustic guitar fingerpicking replaces the electric. The drummer switches to brushes mid-bar. The vocalist drops to a whisper. This extreme sudden drop happens three times in the song, each time more shocking because the listener expects it but it still surprises. After each quiet section of eight bars, the full volume returns just as suddenly. Electric guitar, acoustic guitar, bass, drums, male vocals. 130 BPM in B minor. 4/4 time. Raw rock recording.

test_prompts.title: Al Niente
test_prompts.concept: al niente(무로) — 소리가 완전한 무음까지 점진적으로 사라지는 지시. 데드존 정면 도전
test_prompts.corpus_reference: al niente(0회), fade to nothing(0회), morendo(0회), perdendosi(0회)
test_prompts.sp: Chamber orchestra piece that ends with an extended al niente — a gradual fade to absolute nothing over sixty-four bars. The piece begins with full orchestra at mezzo forte: strings, woodwinds, brass, percussion. Every eight bars, one section drops out and the remaining instruments reduce their volume. First the percussion stops. Then the brass fades away. Then the woodwinds thin to a single flute. Then the upper strings leave one by one. The last sixty-four bars are a solo cello playing a sustained note that decreases in volume so gradually that the listener cannot tell the exact moment the sound ends — it simply dissolves into silence. This is al niente, to nothing. The disappearance should be imperceptible. 60 BPM. Key of G minor. 4/4 time. Concert hall acoustic.

test_prompts.title: Terraced Dynamics
test_prompts.concept: 단계적 다이내믹(계단식 음량) — 바로크 시대 양식. 점진적 변화 없이 섹션 단위로 음량 블록 전환
test_prompts.sp: Baroque-style concerto grosso for harpsichord and strings demonstrating terraced dynamics. In Baroque music, dynamics change in blocks like steps on a staircase, not gradually. The concertino group plays a phrase at forte. The ripieno group immediately echoes the same phrase at piano. No crescendo or decrescendo connects the two levels — the change is instant, like flipping a switch. Section A alternates forte and piano blocks every four bars. Section B uses three levels: forte, mezzo-forte, and piano in a descending terrace. Section C uses the echo effect where the full ensemble plays loud, then a small group repeats the phrase softly as if heard from a distance. Harpsichord, strings. 96 BPM in D major. 4/4 time. Bright, clear recording.

test_prompts.sp: Rock band piece with dramatic volume storytelling. The song starts so quiet you have to strain to hear it. A single guitar string plucked so gently it barely makes a sound. The drums just a fingertip tap on the rim. The bass just a ghost note. Vocals barely a breath. Then the song gets a tiny bit louder. And a tiny bit more. Like sunrise — you cannot see it moving but suddenly it is bright. By the middle of the song, the band plays at a comfortable, normal volume. Then it keeps getting louder. The guitar gets more aggressive. The drums hit harder. The bass drives forward. The vocals push. By the end, the band is playing at the absolute loudest possible volume, every instrument screaming and distorted and overwhelming. Then in one instant, everything drops to a whisper. And then the whisper fades to nothing. 100 BPM in A minor. 4/4 time. Rock production.

test_prompts.title: Articulation Dynamics
test_prompts.concept: 아티큘레이션(staccato/legato/marcato/tenuto)이 다이내믹과 상호작용 — 같은 음량에서 터치 방식의 차이
test_prompts.sp: Piano etude exploring four articulation styles at the same dynamic level mezzo-forte. Section A plays the melody in staccato — every note short, detached, crisp, like raindrops bouncing off a surface. Section B plays the same melody in legato — every note connected smoothly to the next with no gap, singing and flowing. Section C plays in marcato — every note accented and punched, heavy and deliberate, with weight on each attack. Section D plays in tenuto — every note held for its full value with gentle emphasis, sustained and thoughtful. All four sections are at the same volume level, proving that articulation is not dynamics but touch. Solo grand piano. 100 BPM in C major. 4/4 time. Close-miked studio recording.

test_prompts.title: Extreme Dynamic Contrast
test_prompts.concept: 극단적 다이내믹 콘트라스트 — 한 곡 안에서 가능한 최대 음량 범위를 사용. S007 시리즈 종합 스트레스 테스트
test_prompts.sp: Cinematic orchestral piece designed for maximum dynamic range. The piece opens with a single solo violin playing the theme at the absolute softest level, a thread of sound in a vast empty concert hall. Without warning, the full orchestra attacks at maximum fortississimo — one hundred musicians playing the same note at full force. The shock is physical. Then instant silence. The solo violin returns, even softer than before. A solo timpani roll begins at the edge of hearing and swells over thirty-two bars to a thunderous fortissimo. A solo flute plays a melody that is interrupted by sforzando brass stabs — soft melody, explosive punctuation. The final section layers every technique: the orchestra crescendos from nothing to maximum, hits a subito piano, crescendos again, hits sforzando accents randomly, then performs an al niente fade that takes a full minute to reach silence. Full symphony orchestra. 66 BPM in C minor. 4/4 time.
